output.summary: The April OTP decline is real: manual ride checks match AVL, and definitions and equipment are unchanged. It is concentrated where recovery time was cut and where construction lanes were reduced, while the control group (no cut, no construction) shows no decline. The network-wide absence rise is mostly a recording artifact: ShiftLine began automatically capturing partial-day absences, which account for 238 of the 245 added monthly occurrences. Full-day absences are up only 1.1%, and unoperated trips and extraboard use are flat. The proposed discipline policy would penalize the recording change and does not address the mechanisms, and suspending OTP publication would suppress valid data. Recommended: restore recovery on cut routes, set construction running times and work-zone management, and restate absence data by type before any policy decision. The early-leave link to recovery cuts is confounded by seniority, route length and garage.
